newsitem.title: CHINA: China October interest rate subsidy 3.62 pct.
newsitem.headline: China October interest rate subsidy 3.62 pct.

text.p: The People's Bank of China set the interest rate subsidy on deposits of three or more years at 3.62 percent for October, up from 3.61 percent for September, the Financial News said on Saturday.
It was the first time the central bank had raised the deposit rate since April, when it was set at 11.29 percent from 10.83 percent in March.

China said in March it would stop paying interest rate subsidies on deposits of three years and above from April 1 as inflation eased. Falling inflation would enable China to stop paying the subsidy by end-1996 or early next year, state media has said.
Such subsidies would continue to be paid on fixed deposits made before April 1.
On fixed deposits of three, five and eight years, banks currently pay interest rates of 12.24 percent, 14.94 percent and 17.64 percent respectively. The monthly subsidy is paid on top of that.
The subsidy, designed to protect depositors against inflation, was reintroduced in March, 1994, when the rate was 1.19 percent. It hit a record of 13.24 percent in December 1995.
